title: Print method and number of handlers
description:
`fireproof` prints  the number of guards and handlers but the latter is always zero. This is because the private field `handlerMap` is not defined within `fireproof` neither to  super class `Route`. Note that `handlerMap` is  used nevertheless within `Route` class, here
https://github.com/thomasp85/routr/blob/5f12daee832e87247111ab3c9e07d424b4778e7c/R/route.R#L226

Maybe is it `private$routing`?


```r
# From README example

proof
A fireproof plugin with 2 guards and 0 handlers
```

title: `auth` handler accepts only "datastore" as a `STORE_NAME`
description:
The following demos add identical authentication to a path but with different store name. It looks that currently works only on the default case : `"datastore"` name.

### Reprex

<details>
<summary>Click to expand - Source R helpers</summary>

``` r
library(plumber2)
library(mirai)

basic_guard <- fireproof::guard_basic(
  validate = function(username, password) {

    username == "thomas" && password == "pedersen"

  },
  user_info = function(user) {
  fireproof::new_user_info()
  }
)


# api with "datastore" name
demo_api <- function() {

  api <- plumber2::api(port = 8080)
  api <- plumber2::api_datastore(api, storr::driver_environment(),
                                 store_name = "datastore")
  api$add_route("default")

  api <- plumber2::api_auth_guard(api, basic_guard, name = "basicAuth")
  doc_basic <- plumber2::openapi_operation()
  doc_basic$security <- list(list(basicAuth = vector()))


  api <- plumber2::api_post(api,
                            path = "/ping",
                            handler = function(datastore){
                              names(datastore$session$fireproof$basicAuth)
                            },
                            auth_flow = basicAuth,
                            doc = doc_basic,
                            serializers = list("application/json" = plumber2::format_unboxed()))
api
  }

# api with "bamboo" name
demo_api2 <- function() {

  api <- plumber2::api(port = 8000)
  api <- plumber2::api_datastore(api, storr::driver_environment(),
                                 store_name = "bamboo")
  api$add_route("default")

  api <- plumber2::api_auth_guard(api, basic_guard, name = "basicAuth")
  doc_basic <- plumber2::openapi_operation()
  doc_basic$security <- list(list(basicAuth = vector()))


  api <- plumber2::api_post(api,
                            path = "/ping",
                            handler = function(bamboo){
                              names(bamboo$session$fireproof$basicAuth)
                            },
                            auth_flow = basicAuth,
                            doc = doc_basic,
                            serializers = list("application/json" = plumber2::format_unboxed()))
  api
}

api1 <- demo_api()
api2 <- demo_api2()

post_auth <- function(port) {
  uri <- paste0("http://127.0.0.1:", port)
  req <- httr2::request(uri)
  req <- httr2::req_url_path_append(req, "/ping")
  req <- httr2::req_method(req, "post")
  req <- httr2::req_auth_basic(req, "thomas", "pedersen")

  httr2::req_perform(req) |>  httr2::resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE)

}


# run api in a separate process & do not block the current process
mirai::daemons(2)

mi1 <- mirai::mirai({
  api$ignite(block = TRUE, showcase = FALSE)
}, api = api1)



mi2 <- mirai::mirai({
  api$ignite(block = TRUE, showcase = FALSE)
}, api = api2)

```
</details>

```r


# store name: "datastore"
post_auth(8080)
#> [1] "provider" "id"       "name"     "emails"   "photos"   "scopes"

# store name: "bamboo"
post_auth(8000)
#> [1] ""
```

Inspecting a bit further, it seems that `add_auth()` picks the default value "datastore" from this private field:
https://github.com/thomasp85/fireproof/blob/4625feb40544789c1dea97e5d4bf914f42773982/R/Fireproof.R#L298

and is injected here;  note that it cannot be `NULL`  as it is fixed and in addition `firesale` doesn't seem to have `arg_name` field, or it is meant to have one?
https://github.com/thomasp85/fireproof/blob/4625feb40544789c1dea97e5d4bf914f42773982/R/Fireproof.R#L132-L134

Hope I got right the root cause, otherwise apologies!

title: Should  `guard_basic` with invalid credentials return 401 code?
description:
Using  a basic guard with invalid credentials returns always 403 code ( Forbidden). Is it by design? Without creds we get 401 code ( Unauthorized) as expected.

Upon failed authentication, the `check_request()` method assigns an empty list in guard's  fireproof session:

https://github.com/thomasp85/fireproof/blob/4625feb40544789c1dea97e5d4bf914f42773982/R/guard_basic.R#L210

and then the `reject_response()`  method branches out to 403 case:
https://github.com/thomasp85/fireproof/blob/4625feb40544789c1dea97e5d4bf914f42773982/R/guard_basic.R#L224-L226

***

### Reprex

<details>
<summary>Click to expand - Source R helpers</summary>

```r
demo_api <- function(docs = TRUE) {

  basic_guard <- fireproof::guard_basic(
    validate = function(username, password) {
      FALSE  # always invalid credentials
    }
  )

  api <- plumber2::api()
  api <- plumber2::api_datastore(api, storr::driver_environment())
  api$add_route("default")

  api <- plumber2::api_auth_guard(api, basic_guard, name = "basicAuth")

  doc_basic <- plumber2::openapi_operation()
  doc_basic$security <- list(list(basicAuth = vector()))

  api <- plumber2::api_post(api,
                            path = "/authenticate",
                            handler = function() {
                              list(user = "OKish")
                              },
                            auth_flow = basicAuth,
                            doc = doc_basic)

  # run on the background
  if (is.null(mirai::nextget("n"))) {
    mirai::daemons(1L, dispatcher = FALSE, autoexit = tools::SIGINT)
  }

  mi <- mirai::mirai({
    mirai::daemons(1, dispatcher = FALSE)

    if(!docs) {
      # Do not generate API docs
      api$doc_type <- NULL
    }

    api$ignite(block = TRUE, showcase = FALSE)

  },
  docs = docs,
  api = api)

  mi
}


post_login <- function(basic_auth = FALSE) {
  req <- httr2::request("http://127.0.0.1:8080") |>
    httr2::req_url_path_append("/authenticate")

  if (basic_auth) {
    req <-  httr2::req_auth_basic(req, username = "John", password = "none")
  }

  httr2::req_method(req, "post") |>
    httr2::req_perform()
}
```
</details>


```r

# run api on a separate process
mi <- demo_api()

# hit endpoint without providing credentials
post_login(basic_auth = FALSE)
#> Error in `httr2::req_perform()`:
#> ! HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

# hit endpoint with invalid credentials
post_login(basic_auth = TRUE)
#> Error in `httr2::req_perform()`:
#> ! HTTP 403 Forbidden.


# clean up
mirai::stop_mirai(mi)
mirai::daemons(0)
```
